strengths: The row-wise orthogonal updates preserve feasibility exactly, support partial-gradient computation, and admit a useful sufficient-decrease guarantee.
Reducing two-row subproblems to searches over rotations and reflections is a promising approach to nonsmooth optimization on the Stiefel manifold.
The experiments cover three PCA formulations and ten real or synthetic datasets, with several relevant recent baselines and favorable reported objective values.
weaknesses: The central stationarity claim is false under the stated assumptions. Consider h(Y)=||Y||_1, f(Y)=<A,Y>, A=[[0,-2],[0,2],[0,0],[0,0]], and X=[[1,0],[1,0],[0,1],[0,1]]/sqrt(2), with k=2, Q=0, and alpha=2. Every block surrogate has I_2 as its unique global minimizer: each admits a symmetric subgradient certificate with maximum eigenvalue sqrt(2)<alpha. Nevertheless, the squared full stationarity residual from Definition 3.4 equals 2. Thus OBCD can remain at a noncritical point indefinitely, contradicting Theorem 3.8(a), Lemma 4.4(b), and Theorem 4.6. Appendix E.3 incorrectly replaces a potentially different subgradient for each block with one subgradient satisfying all block equations.

The stochastic convergence proofs contain additional substantive gaps. Equation (52) exchanges the previously selected block with a fresh independent block even though the updated iterate depends on the previous selection. Appendix F.4 then uses expectation bounds as pointwise inequalities inside products and removes random quantities from expectations without justification. These steps do not establish the claimed KL-based last-iterate rates.

The main ℓ0 experiments are mathematically degenerate under the stated scaling. Appendix G.2 normalizes ||A||_F=1, giving trace(C)=1 and 0<=trace(X^T C X)<=1. Every tested lambda is at least 10, so adding even one nonzero costs more than any possible variance improvement. Global minimizers therefore have exactly r nonzeros, and the problem reduces to selecting the r largest diagonal entries of C. This inexpensive exact baseline is missing; the experiments do not demonstrate performance on a meaningful sparsity–variance tradeoff.

The exact subproblem solver is incorrect as described. Appendix B lists x_i/y_i as breakpoints of x_i+t*y_i=0, whereas the correct value is -x_i/y_i. It also claims terms with y_i=0 can be discarded, although their ℓ1 contribution, lambda*|x_i|/sqrt(1+t^2), depends on t. These errors require correction and solver verification because the main guarantees assume global subproblem solutions.

The empirical comparisons do not adequately isolate the algorithmic contribution. For ℓ1 SPCA, OBCD receives identity initialization while all competitors receive random initialization. Baseline tuning, repeated-run uncertainty, and ablations of reflections and surrogate choices are not reported. Runtime budgets also differ between the main text and tables. Consequently, the reported gains do not convincingly establish the claimed general superiority.
